title: Is the Stock Market About to SELL-OFF?
creator: Mark Roussin CPA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Mark Roussin flags warning signs beneath record index highs and builds a pullback shopping list. His key breadth stat: only ~35% of S&P 500 stocks sit above their 50-day moving average while the index itself is near all-time highs — narrow participation that often (not always) precedes corrections, echoing 2023's Mag-7-carried market. Other risks: stubborn inflation complicated by surging oil (~$90) and the 10-year Treasury at ~5.24%, a cooling labor market boxing in the Fed, Ray Dalio's AI-bubble warning, credit-market stress, and questions around OpenAI's revenue projections. The consumer is the core worry: nearly 20% of families behind on loan payments (highest since 2010), ~13% of credit-card balances 90+ days delinquent in Q2 2026, and a K-shaped economy where only upper-income spending holds things together. He is not abandoning stocks — a pullback would be a buying opportunity. His shopping list: GOOGL, AVGO, NVDA and MSFT as straightforward buys on a correction; AMD, AMZN and CRDO interest him too but he demands better valuation and sizing (prior conditional buys via puts stand). No explicit calls in this video.
